definition: Most butane is blended with either propane (forming LPG) or gasoline; isobutane is a less-common variant used mainly to raise gasoline octane.
core_idea: Because isobutane is less common than normal butane but has a specific octane-boosting use, it's slightly more valuable, so normal butane is often converted into isobutane to meet that demand.
key_points: Normal butane blended with propane = liquid petroleum gas (LPG).
Normal butane is also blended into gasoline.
Isobutane primarily raises gasoline octane and is less common/more valuable than normal butane.
Normal butane is often converted into isobutane.
relationships: Butane blended with propane forms LPG
trading_implications: Isobutane's scarcity relative to normal butane supports a value premium, incentivizing butane-to-isobutane conversion.
